summary: OpenAI published the model specification for GPT-6 Astra, describing it as its most capable model with a 1.05M token context window, reasoning-effort settings up to 'max', and phased rollout to enterprise Trusted Access customers followed by API and consumer plans.

mechanisms.reason: The lab describes GPT-6 Astra as its most capable model built for the hardest end-to-end work, positioning it as a new frontier tier, though no benchmark figures are given.
mechanisms.quote: GPT-6 Astra is our most capable model, built for the hardest end-to-end work.

mechanisms.reason: The model offers a very large 1.05 million token context window, which raises KV-cache and memory content per accelerator for serving.
Support for reasoning effort up to 'max' implies the model can spend substantially more test-time compute per query, increasing token volume for complex tasks.

practices.reason: A new frontier-tier model with expanded reasoning effort levels, coding and computer-use tool support changes what engineering teams can build interactively and agentically.
practices.quote:
GPT-6 Astra is our most capable model, built for the hardest end-to-end work.
Use it for complex reasoning, coding, computer use, research, and document creation.

practices.reason: New pricing tiers, a large-context surcharge rule, and updated rate-limit tables mean teams evaluating migration must account for cost and quota changes.
practices.quote: Prompts with more than 272K input tokens are priced at 2x input and cache rates and 1.5x output for the full request.
